annotation.title_clean: Ethics for social robotics: A critical analysis
annotation.title_en: Ethics for social robotics: A critical analysis
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Pareto Boada, J.; Román Maestre, B.; Torras, C.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Short workshop paper critiquing the prevailing ethical debate on social assistive robotics for care. Based on a literature review, it identifies three weaknesses (individual-centered focus, narrow concepts of freedom and responsibility, no discussion of teleology) and proposes research lines on freedom, autonomy and justice in care practices.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethics of social assistive robotics is too individual-centered and dyadic in its view of HRI.
Core concepts such as freedom, autonomy and responsibility are understood too narrowly.
The ends (teleology) of care robots are rarely discussed.
Calls for applied ethics and critical theory with a macro perspective of justice.
Proposes research lines on philosophical accounts of freedom/autonomy and on justice.
